items.title: John G. Curran Interview, 1958-05-13
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] Oh. Mr. Kent, he goes in the 20s, 10s, 30s, 10s, and the 40s.

ctx.x: referring back to Celestan's band because he did have a band as far back as 1904. And his band is still going today. With the exception of Celestan, that's the way several years ago. There's been no substitution in his band. And today you couldn't hire that band for the month of December. He's just closed up completely. And a very few times, from the time of David got season open, when he had an open engagement, right on straight through Mardi Gras. And that's supplying right now. It's Mardi Gras, second son,…
Oh. Mr. Kent, he goes in the 20s, 10s, 30s, 10s, and the 40s. Oh yeah. But they always wanted to have a

gig in the top. Always. That's almost standard in New Orleans. Whether the father is in the afternoon or at night. Or at breakfast party in the morning. It's just something that goes west of New Orleans.
